title: Relative torsor representatives and the two boundary signs
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $j:W=T\setminus Z\hookrightarrow T$ its open complement [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $G$ be an abelian etale sheaf [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and let $(P,s)$ be a $G$-torsor with a specified section on $W$ [def-amb-torsor-with-section]. Use the canonical relative class $\alpha(P,s)$ of [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology] and the signed relative complex $C_G^q=I_G^q(T)\oplus I_G^{q-1}(W)$ with differential $D(a,b)=(da,\operatorname{res}(a)-db)$ [def-amb-relative-etale-cohomology]. Form the canonical torsor extension $0\to G\to E_P\to\mathbf Z_T\to0$ of [lem-sc-torsor-h1, def-sc-torsor-extension-presentation]. For any nonnegative injective resolution $G\to I_G^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions] and any extension $h:E_P\to I_G^0$ of its augmentation, let $a\in I_G^1(T)$ be obtained by factoring $dh$ through $\mathbf Z_T$ and evaluating at $1$, and let $b=h(s)\in I_G^0(W)$. Then $\alpha(P,s)$ is represented by $(a,b)$ in this signed cone, independently of $h$ and of the resolution. In particular, for any $g\in G(W)$ the class $\alpha_g$ of the trivial torsor $G$ with specified section $g$ is represented by $(0,g)$, with $g$ inserted in $I_G^0(W)$, and $\alpha_g=-\partial_G^0(g)$, where $\partial_G^q:H^q(W,G)\to H^{q+1}(T,W;G)$ is the localization boundary represented on this cone by $b\mapsto(0,-b)$. More generally, let $0\to G_1\to G_2\to G_3\to0$ be any short exact sequence of abelian etale sheaves, let $g\in G_3(W)$, and let $\delta_W:H^0(W,G_3)\to H^1(W,G_1)$ and $\delta_{T,W}:H^1(T,W;G_3)\to H^2(T,W;G_1)$ be the ordinary and relative connecting maps. With $\alpha_g$ the relative class of $(G_3,g)$, one has $\delta_{T,W}(\alpha_g)=\partial_{G_1}^1(\delta_W(g))$. In degreewise split injective resolutions [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-ses], a lift $r\in I_2^0(W)$ of the cocycle $g$ gives $dr\in I_1^1(W)$ and the two classes in this equality are both represented by $(0,-dr)$. All these identifications are natural under etale restriction of the pair and morphisms of short exact coefficient sequences.
